do_not_conclude: Do not conclude that the instrument can reliably distinguish failed pipeline stage from physical data loss based on authored development cases.

findings.claim: The instrument may be tautological because it uses authored traces and labels, so perfect accuracy is expected and does not validate discrimination between failed pipeline stage and physical data loss.
findings.fix: Add independent adversarial cases where failed pipeline stage and physical data loss produce identical observable traces but different ground truth, and require blind annotation.
findings.why: All cases are authored with exactly one fault per trace and labels are known; the probe checks whether the logic matches the authored fault, not whether it can distinguish ambiguous real-world scenarios.

minimum_next_action: Construct and run a held-out set of adversarial traces with ambiguous evidence for stage failure vs. data loss.

do_not_conclude: Do not conclude that the instrument estimates real localization accuracy from single-fault authored cases alone.

findings.claim: The instrument lacks cases with multiple simultaneous faults, partial evidence, and realistic noise, so internal validity for localization accuracy is limited.
findings.fix: Include multi-fault traces, partial evidence, and noisy provenance in the development set, and report per-fault localization accuracy separately.
findings.why: The fault contract specifies exactly one authored fault per trace, which does not reflect real-world multi-fault scenarios and may overestimate localization accuracy.

minimum_next_action: Expand the development set to include multi-fault and noisy traces before estimating localization accuracy.

do_not_conclude: Do not conclude that B3 outperforms B1/B2 in retrieval or entity resolution; it only measures the ceiling of temporal scoping.

findings.claim: B3 receives oracle history_id and as_of_version, giving it an unfair advantage over B1/B2 which must infer entity and time; the comparison is not fair.
findings.fix: Provide B1/B2 with the same oracle entity and time information, or remove oracle inputs from B3 and require it to infer them from the data.
findings.why: B3 is provided with ground-truth entity and temporal scoping, while B1/B2 are not; thus B3's perfect recall is expected and does not demonstrate superiority in entity resolution or temporal scoping.

minimum_next_action: Re-run the comparison with B3 receiving no oracle history_id or as_of_version, or with B1/B2 receiving the same oracle inputs.

do_not_conclude: Do not conclude that B1/B2 have a fundamental recall limitation at higher k based on this templated corpus.

findings.claim: The observed recall curve for B1/B2 (perfect at k=1,2,4 but zero at k=8,16,...) is likely an artifact of the templated corpus and query design, not a meaningful property of the backends.
findings.fix: Use a larger, more diverse corpus with fuzzy queries and graded relevance to produce meaningful recall curves.
findings.why: With only four templated histories and queries that match exact strings, recall is binary: either the exact match is in the top-k or not. The curve shape is an artifact of the small corpus and exact-match queries.

minimum_next_action: Redesign the retrieval evaluation with a larger corpus and non-exact queries to avoid binary recall artifacts.

do_not_conclude: Do not conclude any architecture or method is effective based on development-only results.

findings.claim: The development instrument uses authored labels and oracle inputs, so perfect scores are not evidence of generalization; the next gate must use independent held-out data.
findings.fix: Create a held-out test set with independent annotation and run the instrument without oracle inputs to measure true performance.
findings.why: All evidence is marked as authored, not held out, and independent annotation is false; thus the instrument only validates the authored logic, not real-world performance.

minimum_next_action: Run the instrument on a held-out, independently annotated dataset without oracle inputs.
